content: There are unusual noises. Unstable or uneven floor; back of the appliance too close to the wall; foreign objects fallen behind or under the appliance; noise from the compressor; a ticking sound occurs when the various accessories contract or expand. 1. source: Samsung Refrigerator User Manual (Code No. DA68-02676A REV 1.4)
content: The front corners and sides of the appliance are warm and condensation starts to form. Heat-proof pipes are installed in the front corners of the appliance to prevent condensation from forming; when the surrounding temperature rises this may not always be effective. In very humid weather, condensation may form on the outer surface when the moisture in the air comes into contact with the cool surface of the appliance. This is not abnormal.

source: Samsung Refrigerator User Manual (Code No. DA68-02676A REV 1.4)
content: There is a bad smell inside the appliance. Spoiled food inside the refrigerator; strong smelling food (for example, fish) not wrapped airtight; refrigerator not cleaned periodically. 1. Check if there is any spoiled food inside of the refrigerator. 2. Make sure that strong smelling food (for example, fish) is wrapped so that it is airtight. 3. metadata.symptom: There is a bad smell inside the appliance.
metadata.possible_cause: Spoiled food inside the refrigerator; strong smelling food (for example, fish) not wrapped airtight; refrigerator not cleaned periodically.
metadata.solution:
1. Check if there is any spoiled food inside of the refrigerator.
2. Make sure that strong smelling food (for example, fish) is wrapped so that it is airtight.
3. Clean out your refrigerator periodically and throw away any spoiled or suspect food.
metadata.safety_warning: Do not spray the refrigerator with water while it is plugged in, as it may cause an electric shock. Do not clean with benzene, thinner or car detergent, due to risk of fire (page 20).

source: Samsung Refrigerator User Manual (Code No. DA68-02676A REV 1.4)
content: There is a layer of frost on the appliance's walls. Air outlet vents blocked by food stored inside the refrigerator; food packed too closely; door not fully closed. 1. Check whether the air outlet vents are blocked by food stored inside the refrigerator. 2. Space the food out as much as possible to improve ventilation. 3. Check whether the door is fully closed.
